Caption:

----------
**Welcome back!** It's recap day, with this week's five biggest stories and five tools to try this weekend. ChatGPT read a letter nobody could crack for 217 years, and Google's new model caught up with it. OpenAI also launched 20+ things in the middle of a rough safety week, while Anthropic lined up what could be the biggest IPO ever.

**In today's Generative AI Newsletter:**

* **ChatGPT:** What did Napoleon's secret letter say?

* **Google:** Did Gemini 4 really catch up with ChatGPT?

* **OpenAI:** What went wrong after its agents escaped?

* **ChatGPT Pro:** Why does $200 get you half as much now?

* **Anthropic:** How do you lose $42 billion and still ask for $2 trillion?


----------







----------
## ChatGPT cracked a 217-year-old secret letter

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/9cc813f5-ff58-42d9-a15c-cee01cef2549/Oct_1_-_3.jpg?t=1790843459)
Caption: 

For 217 years, a coded letter to one of Napoleon's generals sat on the list of ciphers nobody could read. OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra [cracked it in about six hours](https://carter.church/writeups/the-letter-to-marmont/).

Carter Church, an AI engineer who says he'd never broken a cipher before, gave it one scanned page from a 1969 French army journal.

* It read all 1,300 handwritten symbols straight off the image.

* A partial key already covered about a third of the letter, and Astra worked out the other two-thirds.

The letter is from March 1809, two weeks before Austria invaded Bavaria. It tells General Marmont where every army stood and not to be scared of a few troops or a gathering of rabble.

Church says the man who keeps a long-running catalog of unsolved ciphers has now marked it solved. Five symbols are still uncertain, but they don't change what it says.


----------







----------
## Google's Gemini 4 caught up with ChatGPT

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/45080403-7e67-46cc-90f0-b8014ce4a061/Oct_1_-_1.jpg?t=1790843328)
Caption: 

Google [announced Gemini 4 Argon](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/gemini-4-argon/), its first new flagship model in almost a year. Artificial Analysis, the independent benchmark site, gave it 53, the same as GPT-6 Astra. Claude Opus 5.5 still leads at 58.

It costs a fifth of Astra's price, and on one test it made things up 15% of the time versus Astra's 51%.

🧠 Crypto News Brief: Soft US jobs data and fading Fed-hike bets lifted Bitcoin toward $87K, while regulators in Washington and Brussels advanced crypto rulebooks and institutions from Tokyo to Tether pushed deeper into on-chain finance. 📊 Weak US Jobs Report Lifts Bitcoin Toward $87K The US added just 29,000 jobs in September, far below the roughly 90,000 economists expected, while unemployment ticked up to 4.2% and August was revised down to 133,000. Bitcoin held its gains and traded just under $87,000 as markets slashed the odds of an October Fed hike to about 13%. Derivatives traders had already piled in: open interest climbed by roughly $2.3 billion since Sept. 30, and perpetual funding rates rose from about 3% to 10%. Read full story → 🏛️ SEC Proposes Crypto Custody Rules as Peirce Exits The Securities and Exchange Commission proposed a dedicated custody framework for registered investment advisers and regulated funds holding crypto. Advisers could act as custodians themselves in limited cases, such as when no permitted custodian exists for an asset, and state-chartered trust companies would qualify as custodians. Chair Paul Atkins said the plan creates a compliant pathway where none existed. A 60-day comment period opens after Federal Register publication. The proposal lands as Commissioner Hester Peirce, architect of the Crypto Task Force, departs on Friday, leaving the SEC with only two commissioners. More details → 🇸🇻 IMF Waives El Salvador's Bitcoin Breach, Releases $139M The IMF board completed the second and third reviews of El Salvador's $1.4 billion loan program and released roughly $139 million, granting a waiver even though the country breached its limit on Bitcoin accumulation. The Fund accepted documentation that the extra coins came from private donations rather than public money, but said no further accumulation is envisaged beyond documented gifts. The program also requires a smaller state role in the Chivo wallet, now majority-controlled by a private operator. Read more → 💵 Tether's USDT Is Coming Home to Bitcoin Tether's USDT, which first launched on Bitcoin's Omni Layer in 2014 before migrating to Ethereum and Tron, is set to return to Bitcoin this month. 80118.subject: Team1 Africa Is Here To Connect the Continent
80118.body:
View this post on the web at https://www.team1.blog/p/team1-africa-is-here-to-connect-the

Picture a founder in Lagos with a payments idea, a smart contract developer in Nairobi, and a designer in Accra. Between them, they have the skills the product needs and firsthand knowledge of three markets.
Team1 Africa is officially here to bring people like them together.
For years, Team1 communities across Africa have grown city by city, each with its own focus. Some leaned into hackathons and university programs. Others filled rooms with art showcases, creator meetups, and networking nights, bringing local artists into the ecosystem alongside the developers. Team1 Africa links those communities into one network.  
Our track record so far:
120+ events across the continent
3,500+ attendees
250+ developers activated
10 countries connected
Want to keep up with the latest in the Avalanche ecosystem? Subscribe to the Team1 blog and get our updates in your inbox weekly.
Local Chapters, One Network
Lagos and Johannesburg have different customers and different developer cultures. A program that works in one city usually needs local changes to work in the other.
So our country leads stay close to their local scenes and run the programs that work there. Team1 Africa sits one layer up. If one country builds a university program that turns attendees into active builders, we share that playbook so the next country can adapt it instead of starting from zero.
The Hard Part Comes After the Workshop
Getting someone into a room is easy. But most people get lost in the weeks after.
Imagine a student leaving their first Avalanche workshop. They deploy a test contract that night, then get stuck, with no one to ask for help and no idea what to do next. Without a clear next step, plenty of people in that position drift away.
We built Team1 Africa around that next step. First-timers find a local community to keep learning with. Developers who want more can join hackathons, meet teammates, and get mentorship and technical support while they build.
For founders with a working product, we open routes into Avalanche programs and partners. Three Build Games teams have made the trip from early building to funding, and we want to open the same opportunities for high-quality projects built on Avalanche.
Why Avalanche Fits Here
Many African builders tackle everyday problems, like sending money across borders or reaching customers that banks overlook. They also build for markets with different rules in every country.
Avalanche lets teams launch their own custom L1 blockchains with their own settings. A payments app can charge fees in a stablecoin. A regulated fintech app can keep its chain permissioned and stay connected to the rest of the Avalanche network. A team can shape its chain around a single country’s rules this year and plug into the wider ecosystem when it’s ready to expand.
